answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can submit jobs, then slash that stake when a randomly sampled, independently verified task fails. Splitting one identity into a hundred does not multiply the attacker’s stake: each account must fund its own bond, and useful influence still depends on passing the same checks. A ferrous sensor report or a cedar shipment claim is evidence only if verified; a fable earns no payout. The attacker pays capital costs upfront and risks losing it per lie.
